properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-09-22: the flow "concept/ideas → requirements → capabilities… kind of ends there. Instead, it should continue with capabilities → tested / verified / validated → fully fielded / operational."

⭐ FIRST, A CORRECTION WORTH MAKING BEFORE BUILDING ANYTHING: THE RUNGS EXIST. `Capability.status` runs planned → in_progress → realized → verified, and `maturity_report` already reports seven bands — intent, function, allocation, seams, realization, assurance, operation — with operation computed from a release's DEPLOYED_TO edge. The ladder he describes is modelled and read today.

🛑 WHAT IS MISSING IS THE DRIVE. A capability reads `verified` because a session typed it. Nothing moves it there because a run said so, and nothing moves it BACK when a run stops saying so. Measured the same day: 311 checks read `passing`, **none has ever read `failing`**, and 282 cannot be re-run at all. A status that can only go up, set by the same agent that wrote the code, is a claim wearing a lifecycle's clothes.

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN.

(a) STATUS IS DERIVED, NEVER STORED — `verified` is computed from "has a check with an executable form whose last run passed", the way the delivery line is already computed from the thread rather than read off a field. ⭐ Consistent with `dec:certainty-derived`, which already does exactly this for Requirement certainty. ⚠️ Counter: it makes a status unsettable by hand, which breaks the non-code case where a person IS the evidence.

(b) A STATUS ADVANCE REQUIRES EVIDENCE IN THE SAME CALL — `set_capability_status(verified)` refuses without naming the run that justifies it, the way a settling status already refuses without an approver. ⭐ The precedent is exact and recent. ⚠️ Counter: it is a refusal on a path used constantly, and refusals on hot paths get routed around.

(c) THE LADDER CAN GO DOWN. Today nothing demotes. If a check starts failing, the capability that claimed `verified` on it should stop claiming it — that is the half that makes the ladder mean anything, and it is worth more than any of the promotion mechanics. ⚠️ Counter: needs ① of the founding chain working first, since nothing currently records a failure.

(d) NOTHING — accept that a status is an assertion and make the REPORTS honest instead, separating "claimed verified" from "verified by a run that can be re-run". Cheapest, and it is what `graph_report` half does already. ⚠️ Counter: leaves the number that drew the criticism exactly where it is.
properties.name: OPEN — the rungs from realized to verified to fielded already exist. Nothing DRIVES a capability up them on evidence, so a status is typed rather than earned
properties.rationale: Recorded because the obvious reading of his sentence — "build the missing rungs" — would produce vocabulary that already exists and leave the actual defect untouched. The rungs are there; what is absent is anything that makes a status a consequence of evidence rather than a note. Option (c) is listed because a ladder that cannot go down is not a lifecycle, and it is the half nobody asks for.
